caption: SWR — a measure of how well a load is matched to a transmission line (T9B12) — is lowest at the antenna's resonant frequency, where 1:1 means a perfect match between antenna and feed line. Away from resonance, reflected power climbs and the reading rises toward a mismatch like 4:1. It matters because high SWR makes a solid-state transceiver reduce its output power to protect the RF output transistors (T7B04).
spoken: a curve of SWR versus frequency across the two-meter band, dipping to one-to-one at the resonant frequency and rising toward the band edges
